correctness.rationale: Inspecting pinned RESULT.md and verify.py: O(d+1) averaging preserves P_1 reproduction and P_2 range, and multiplicity-free harmonic decomposition leaves one scalar degree-two coefficient b. N_d(b)=E|1+(d+1)u+b((d+1)u²-1)|. Integrating against sign(u) gives the exact fixed first-harmonic lower bound; equality forces K(0)=0 so b=1. Beta integral gives the Gamma constant. Expanding the exactly identifiable wrong-sign intervals around u=0 and, for δ>0, u=-1 gives origin c_d δ²/(d+1) and endpoint B_d δ_+^(d/2+1), with stated remainder. The unital-operator negative mass identity explains (Lambda-1)/2. Independent split-at-real-roots quadrature agrees for d=1,2,3,5,10; in d=2 sides at δ=0.0005 are 0.166685 and 0.832797, compared with 1/6 and 5/6. The all-d proof is analytical, not deduced from these five computations.

originality.rationale: PASS best of knowledge for the no-cost unital extension with degree-two free multiplier and asymmetric stability cusp, NOT for the bare Gamma numerical constant: by Rutovitz classical projection constant for real Euclidean space (quoted as Eq. (5) of Defant et al. 2026) equals this Gamma expression when n=d+1. Critical distinction: a projection onto first harmonics annihilates constants, while this operator must reproduce constants and first harmonics; projections onto all P_2 force degree-two multiplier 1 rather than 2/(d+3). Wu gives symmetry reduction and order bounds, but no full-text available to certify absence of an equivalent first-band special case; named risk retained.

value.rationale: The first genuine transition bandwidth (degree-one exact reproduction with degree-two output) is a canonical multivariate approximation problem; an explicit minimizer attains the classical linear-space constant while preserving constants and the dimension-dependent nonsmooth endpoint stability differentiates circle, ordinary sphere and higher dimensions. This is a sharp useful boundary, not mere rewriting of Rutovitz's known Gamma number.

final_claim: Every real bounded map C(S^d)->P_2 reproducing P_1 has norm at least (d+1)Gamma((d+1)/2)/(sqrt(pi)Gamma((d+2)/2)), attained by the quadratic zonal kernel (d+1)u(1+u), uniquely among equivariant maps; its one-parameter equivariant stability deficit has an antipodal one-sided exponent d/2+1.
limitations: Fixed integer d≥1; one-parameter stability only for equivariant multipliers; no global stability among arbitrary nonsymmetric admissible maps; finite quadratures alone not proof.
